a1.say: Let's solve Least-Frequently-Used Cache, using the Frequency Buckets approach.

a1.cap: Build LFUCache(capacity) with O(1) get(key) (value or -1) and put(key, value). When full, put of a new key evicts the key used the fewest times; among ties, evict the least recently used. A new key starts with one use.
a1.say: Build LFUCache(capacity) with O of one get(key) (value or minus 1) and put(key, value). When full, put of a new key evicts the key used the fewest times; among ties, evict the least recently used. A new key starts with one use.

lines: Build LFUCache(capacity) with O(1) get(key) (value or -1) and put(key, value). When full, put of a new key evicts the key used the fewest times; among ties, evict the least recently used. A new key starts with one use.

a1.cap: For example, with the calls LFUCache(2), put(1, 1), put(2, 2), get(1), put(3, 3), get(2), get(3), put(4, 4), get(1), get(3), get(4), the answer is [null,null,null,1,null,-1,3,null,-1,3,4].
a1.say: For example, with the calls LFUCache(2), put(1, 1), put(2, 2), get(1), put(3, 3), get(2), get(3), put(4, 4), get(1), get(3), get(4), the answer is null, null, null, 1, null, -1, 3, null, -1, 3, 4.

lines: Input: the calls LFUCache(2), put(1, 1), put(2, 2), get(1), put(3, 3), get(2), get(3), put(4, 4), get(1), get(3), get(4)

a1.cap: Keep each key's value and use count, plus one ordered bucket per count holding keys from least to most recent. Track min_freq, the smallest count present.
a1.say: Keep each key's value and use count, plus one ordered bucket per count holding keys from least to most recent. Track min freq, the smallest count present.

a1.cap: A use moves a key from bucket f to bucket f + 1. Eviction removes the oldest key in the min_freq bucket.
a1.say: A use moves a key from bucket f to bucket f plus 1. Eviction removes the oldest key in the min freq bucket.

a1.cap: Let's walk through it with the calls LFUCache(2), put(1, 1), put(2, 2), get(1), put(3, 3), get(2), get(3), put(4, 4), get(1), get(3), get(4).
Key 1 is used again; its count rises to 2.
Full: evict key 2, the least frequently used.
Key 3 is used again; its count rises to 2.
Full: evict key 1, the least frequently used.
Key 3 is used again; its count rises to 3.
Key 4 is used again; its count rises to 2.
Time complexity is O(1) per call and extra space is O(capacity).
a1.say: Time complexity is O of one per call and extra space is O of capacity.

a1.cap: That's the Frequency Buckets approach. Now try writing it yourself, in Java or Python!
